meta.coord_system_note: coord_system = lab selects the energy network's input frame (absolute).

estimator.name: response_ratio
estimator.definition: R = E_est / p per event; σ/E = s(R)/R̄ per momentum window, in percent, with s the unbiased (ddof = 1) sample SD.
estimator.label: σ(R)/μ(R), R = E_est / p

top.name: Energy (GeV) ⟶
top.rule: E = 1/x², an exact relabelling of the bottom axis; no data are plotted against it.

energy.rule: E = 1/x² of the 1/√E view's x = ⟨1/√p⟩: one exact bijection, so both views draw the same measurements.
notes: The E view's y range follows the windows with N ≥ 20 from 2 GeV (whiskers included) and the a/√E ⊕ b and a₀/√E fits over the windows each was fitted to, from zero; a window below 2 GeV never sets it.
Fitted curves are drawn from 4 GeV, the lowest window edge any fit can use, to 80 GeV: solid over the windows each fit ran through, dashed beyond, where the curve extrapolates its form.

Each window is drawn at E = 1/x² with x = ⟨1/√p⟩, the abscissa the fits used, so a window on its fitted line in the 1/√E view sits on its fitted curve here; its ⟨p⟩, slightly larger (Jensen's inequality), is in its tooltip.

anchors.rule: Chosen on the whole table's bins, not the selection: the lowest bin from 5 GeV, the highest bin, and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres. A series whose anchor holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20, named in substitutions; with fewer than two, windows of N ≥ 8 and the fit is provisional.

notes: Each shower's deposit E_dep is the truth segmentation's share of the event's hit energy (a cell both showers hit is divided by the truth fraction) and p is that shower's own incident momentum. Showers A and B are separate series with one value per event each; an event in which a shower has no hit rows is not part of that shower's series.

Each window is the producer's integer momentum bin k, [k, k + 1) GeV, of the shower's own momentum. Per event R = E_est / p; the plotted value is σ/E = s(R)/R̄ in percent (s with ddof = 1), its whisker the 95% χ² interval of s divided by R̄ (N − 1 d.o.f.; R̄'s own uncertainty is neglected, the delta-method se_delta includes it), and its abscissa x = ⟨1/√p⟩ over the window's events. Dividing by p event by event removes the window's own momentum spread and the estimator's bias, and c cancels in s(R)/R̄, so the detector series does not depend on the calibration.
The detector series c·E_dep is a linear-sum benchmark, not a limit: a model that reads the shower's shape (leakage, compensation) can do better than a plain sum.
E on both axes is the incident momentum p as the producer writes it. For a massive species √(p² + m²) differs from p by at most m²/2p², 1.7% for a proton at 5 GeV/c.
σ/E is reported from N = 2; a window is drawn with its whisker from N = 8, and enters the fits and sets the y range from N = 20 and p ≥ 4 GeV.

Fits: a/√E + b and a₀/√E through the origin, by weighted least squares with weights 1/se², se the delta-method standard error of σ/μ recomputed at the fitted value and iterated (half steps once the refits oscillate); χ², ν = n − p and its p-value. Where χ²/ν > 1 the standard errors and the 95% band are scaled by S = √(χ²/ν) (PDG), and the band then takes Student's t₀.₉₇₅,ν rather than 1.96, since S is estimated from the fit's own ν. The band is the 95% confidence band of the line, not the spread of the events. The quadrature form √(a²/E + b²) is fitted as (σ/E)² = A/E + B and tabled, not drawn; its b and the affine b are different constant terms.

Anchors: the lowest bin from 5 GeV (below it the sampling fraction is still rising), the highest bin and the bin between them nearest in log E to the geometric mean of their centres, chosen on the whole table so they do not move with the selection. A series whose anchor window holds N < 20 takes its nearest window from 5 GeV in log E with N ≥ 20 instead; with fewer than two such windows its fit runs through windows of N ≥ 8 and is provisional. The other mode fits every window with N ≥ 20 from 4 GeV, the 4–5 GeV window included, below the anchors' floor.
The top axis is an exact relabelling of the bottom one, E = 1/x²: a deterministic unit conversion, and no data are plotted against it.
Shower A: c = Σ p / Σ E_dep = 138.3 over N = 286 events, fitted once over the whole selection.
Shower B: c = Σ p / Σ E_dep = 136.1 over N = 286 events, fitted once over the whole selection.
The model series is the energy network of the absolute frame (coord_system), R = predicted energy / its truth; the networks predict the momentum scale directly, with no calibration.
Off the axis: 8 windows below 4 GeV (164 events across the series) have x > 0.5; they are listed in off_axis with their σ/E and not drawn.
